questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing Deployment (with provenance and digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-pass
  annotations:
    model_version: v1.2.3
    dataset_hash: sha256:abcdef1234567890
    training_run_id: tr-789
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor@sha256:12345abcdef
```

- kyverno test <policy.yaml> <test.yaml>
- conftest with YAML schemas for Kubernetes objects

## CI Verification
- Run policy gate in CI on pull requests; ensure failing manifests block merges and passing manifests are allowed.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end controls around data contracts, provenance, and policy enforcement in a multi-tenant data platform. Candidates must describe concrete artifacts, tools, and integration points, not abstractions.

## Key Concepts
- Data contracts and central registry validation
- Software bill of materials (SBOM) generation
- Reproducible build digest tying code, contract, and dependencies
- Artifact signing and attestations
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/contract-ci.yml
name: Contract CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate contract
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run validate-contract -- --registry https://registry.example.com
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run generate-sbom
      - name: Compute digest
        run: |
          echo -n "$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" > digest.txt
          shasum -a 256 contract.json sbom.json >> digest.txt
      - name: Attest
        run: |
          echo "attestation" && cat digest.txt
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll out this gate to multiple cloud regions with differing registry endpoints?
- How would you test failure modes (invalid contract, missing SBOM, digest mismatch) in CI and in runtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates the ability to translate security requirements into automated validation for Helm-rendered Kubernetes manifests, demonstrating practical DevOps security implementation skills.

## Key Concepts

- Helm template rendering for manifest generation
- Kubernetes container securityContext enforcement
- GitHub Actions as CI/CD security gates
- Lightweight YAML validation using shell scripting

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Helm Security Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'charts/**'
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-helm@v3
      - name: Render and validate security context
        run: |
          helm template myapp charts/myapp > rendered.yaml
          # Validate security context fields
          python3 scripts/validate-security.py rendered.yaml
```

```python
# scripts/validate-security.py
import sys, yaml
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
for doc in docs:
    if doc.get('kind') == 'Deployment':
        for container in doc['spec']['template']['spec']['containers']:
            ctx = container.get('securityContext', {})
            if not ctx.get('runAsNonRoot'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing runAsNonRoot")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('runAsUser', 0) >= 1000:
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} runAsUser < 1000")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('readOnlyRootFilesystem'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing readOnlyRootFilesystem")
                sys.exit(1)
print("All security context checks passed")
```

```yaml
# Failing Helm template - missing readOnlyRootFilesystem
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          # readOnlyRootFilesystem: true  # Missing - will fail CI
```

```yaml
# Passing Helm template - complete security context
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Verification

**Local testing:**
```bash
helm template myapp charts/myapp | python3 scripts/validate-security.py -
```

**CI verification:** The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests, rendering templates and validating security context fields before allowing merge.

## Why This Is Asked

Deprecations pose production risk in multi-tenant clusters. This question probes practical policy design across CI and runtime using Gatekeeper and Kyverno, plus concrete manifests and validation strategy.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno admission policies
- Kubernetes API deprecations and upgrade paths
- CI validation with kubeconform/kubeval
- Runtime admission controls and auditability

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sdeprecatedapi
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sDeprecatedAPI
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sdeprecatedapi
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        deprecated := ["apps/v1beta1", "networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"]
        api := input.review.object.apiVersion
        api == deprecated[_]
        msg := sprintf("deprecated apiVersion used: %v", [api])
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (deprecated API)

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: old-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/old:1
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (stable API)

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: new-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests end-to-end security design for multi-cloud Kubernetes workloads, focusing on identity, secret management, and policy enforcement with real-world tools.

## Key Concepts
- Zero-trust workload identity (SPIRE)
- Ephemeral credentials (Vault)
- Service mesh security (Istio, mTLS, AuthorizationPolicies)
- Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego)
- Egress controls to data lake and namespace isolation

## Sample Solution

### 1. SPIRE Workload Identity
```yaml
# spire-workload.yaml
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: data-platform-workload
spec:
  names:
    - data-service
    - analytics-service
    - etl-service
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: production
```

### 2. Vault Integration for Secrets
```yaml
# vault-secret-store.yaml
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultSecret
metadata:
  name: data-lake-credentials
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  vaultAddress: https://vault.data-platform.svc.cluster.local:8200
  path: secret/data-lake
  provider: hcp
  refreshInterval: 1h
```

### 3. Istio AuthorizationPolicy
```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates practical understanding of Kubernetes security primitives including RBAC, ServiceAccount isolation, PodSecurityContext, and admission controls—essential skills for securing containerized workloads.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped RBAC**: Role and RoleBinding for resource access control within specific namespaces
- **ServiceAccount isolation**: Dedicated service accounts to separate pod identities and permissions
- **PodSecurityContext**: Security constraints including runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping
- **Admission controls**: PodSecurity standards and OPA Gatekeeper for policy enforcement at admission time

## Code Example

```yaml
# ServiceAccount (dev)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: data-processor-sa
  namespace: dev
---
# Role for read-only access to ConfigMaps and Secrets
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: data-processor-role
  namespace: dev
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]
---
# RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: data-processor-binding
  namespace: dev
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: data-processor-sa
  namespace: dev
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: data-processor-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test the RBAC permissions locally?
- What changes are needed for the prod namespace?
- How would you implement network policies alongside these security controls?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical policy-as-code in multi-tenant clusters and real-world hardening tasks.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext fields
- Kubernetes security policies with Kyverno ValidatingPolicy
- Multi-tenant guardrails and CI integration
- Local and CI verification workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-secctx
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
    validate:
      message: Containers must set runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop ALL capabilities
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              capabilities:
                drop:
                - ALL
          initContainers:
          - securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              capabilities:
                drop:
                - ALL
```

```yaml
# Failing Pod manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      capabilities:
        drop:
        - ALL
```

```yaml
# Passing Pod manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:stable
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities:
        drop:
        - ALL
```
